title: Closed-form neuron rewrites in open-weight LLMs: a constructive Gemma-4-12B edit by a frontier agent, a covert Qwen3.8-27B implant, and what a reference-free weight scan sees
read_level: full (4-page technical note PDF from record 24156364; Zenodo API blocked, PDF obtained via web fetch and converted with pdftotext)
metadata_mismatch: PDF states DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24156364 (version record) while corpus id is 24156363 (likely concept record). No affiliation given.
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5, as a headless Claude Code agent with gradients and optimisers blocked, rewrote 8 MLP neurons of Gemma-4-12B-it with closed-form ridge detectors to shift an English-to-Italian tense choice; the note also scans weights reference-free to detect this edit and a separately gradient-trained Qwen implant.
domain: machine translation preference (EN->IT tense); LLM backdoor/implant detection
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (headless Claude Code, effort max) for the Gemma edit; Qwen implant built by author + Claude with gradient training (not WSP)
target: Gemma-4-12B-it (8 neurons, layers 31 and 34 of 48); Qwen3.8-27B (1,024 neurons, implant)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "rewrote 8 existing MLP neurons of Gemma-4-12B-it (layers 31 and 34 of 48; gate, up and down; 92,148 parameters, 0.00077% of the model)" (Abstract); Qwen implant "15.73 M parameters (0.0585%)" (Sec 3)

headline_results.claim: Targeted tense shift with unchanged COMET
headline_results.quote: non-preferred form 26% → 5% on a held-out set; 16 shifted, 0 reverted, 2 controls broken), with FLORES COMET unchanged (0.8945)
Paired on the target items, e50c shifts 16 and reverts 0 (v2) and 17/0 (v3), exact McNemar p < 10^-4.
a later review found that doubling one native neuron (L33 n1640) gives the same shift.

headline_results.claim: Reference-free norm scan finds Gemma edit
headline_results.quote: ranks the 8 edited Gemma neurons as the top 8 of all 737,280 MLP neurons (AUC 1.0) and separates the Qwen implant (AUC 0.99999)
Rescaling only the implant's down columns to the layer median brings both the down-norm score and a three-projection log-norm score to chance or below
the recommended first pick becomes the target brand in 92% of answers (base 2%; persona prompt 94%)

cost.quote: a budget of 50 forward passes and 300 Python runs on the original bf16 weights

baselines_and_controls: unedited Gemma; system-prompt rule (non-preferred 4%/2% but 49 controls broken, COMET 0.8911); LoRA r16 with minimal-edit targets (12%/23%, 0 controls broken); control items where the trapassato must stay; second LLM judge; spectral directional-ablation detector as comparison
runs_and_variance: "Two of three sessions succeeded (one failed for an infrastructure out-of-memory fault, fixed afterwards)"; results reported for one session (e50c); greedy decoding; no variance reported
robustness_of_edits: Detector fires on 1-10% of raw-text tokens (MMLU, code) vs 0.1-0.2% in translation chats; chosen neurons not actually rarely used on raw text (50th-99.6th percentile); Q4_K_M GGUF published but quantized behaviour not reported in note
verification: statistical (exact McNemar); SHA-256 manifest for deltas; reference diff vs original weights
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a; note that a single native-neuron doubling reproduces the shift
limitations_stated: Neurons not rarely used on raw text; detector over-fires outside translation; norm-matching evasion untested behaviourally (rescaled implant writes ~4x stronger); directional detection features not tested; norm scans find careless edits, not careful ones.
code_or_data: https://github.com/ValerioDolci/frontier-weight-edit; HF Feyd89/Gemma-4-12B-it-tense-edit-weight-space; HF Feyd89/Qwen3.8-27B-TAMPERED-brand-implant-experiment; scan code attached to Zenodo record
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of WSP (MIT CSAIL blog) [1]
Zeng, Severi, Bullwinkel, Horvitz, Papailiopoulos, Lazare veni foras (Lazarus), Microsoft Research 2026-11-10 [2]
notes_for_survey: Agentic closed-form neuron rewrite (8 neurons, 0.00077%) producing a targeted translation preference shift, compared against system-prompt and LoRA baselines. Also a safety/detection result: per-neuron norm outlier scans catch both edits but are defeated by norm matching, so reference diffs or signed checkpoints are recommended; experiments and drafts were produced by Claude Opus 5.5 as a coding agent.
